## Summary

The repository is the **Spring PetClinic REST** sample. All owner-creation business rules (including `householdId`, `namesakeCount`, `customerCode`, `bulkSignupWarning`) are computed in the **V1 REST controller**, while `membershipTier` is a *derived getter* on the `Owner` entity. Importantly, **the GOLD tier logic does not yet exist** — see note at the end.

---

### 1. Where `membershipTier` is computed (BRONZE / SILVER / GOLD)

**File:** `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java` (lines 185-193)

```java
/**
 * The owner's membership tier: {@code 'SILVER'} when namesakeCount is 0 and an email is
 * present, otherwise {@code 'BRONZE'}.
 */
public String getMembershipTier() {
    boolean unique = this.namesakeCount != null && this.namesakeCount == 0;
    boolean hasEmail = this.email != null && !this.email.isEmpty();
    return unique && hasEmail ? "SILVER" : "BRONZE";
}
```

This is a **computed, read-only** property (no backing DB column, no setter). It is derived purely from `namesakeCount` and `email`. **There is currently NO GOLD logic anywhere in `src/main`** — only SILVER and BRONZE are ever returned. GOLD appears only in the acceptance test expectation (see item 5).

The property is exposed in the API contract at `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/openapi.yml` (lines 2150-2157), which drives the generated `OwnerDto`. The description there also only mentions SILVER/BRONZE.

---

### 2. The `Owner` entity — all fields

**File:** `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java` (extends `Person`, which supplies `id`, `firstName`, `lastName`)

Persisted `@Column` fields (lines 39-72):
- `address` (`@NotEmpty`)
- `city` (`@NotEmpty`)
- `telephone` (`@NotEmpty`, `@Pattern` E.164)
- `email` (`@Email`; setter lower-cases it, line 103)
- `registrationDate` (`LocalDate`, column `registration_date`)
- `customerCode` (column `customer_code`)
- **`householdId`** (column `household_id`, lines 62-63)
- `namesakeCount` (`Integer`, column `namesake_count`)
- `bulkSignupWarning` (`Boolean`, column `bulk_signup_warning`)
- `pets` (`@OneToMany`)

Derived (computed, non-persisted) getters:
- `getDisplayName()` (line 149)
- `getInitials()` (line 157)
- `getMembershipNumber()` (line 166)
- `getLocality()` (line 181, uses the `CITY_REGION` map at line 171)
- **`getMembershipTier()`** (line 189)

`householdId` has a standard getter/setter (lines 122-128). `membershipTier` has only a getter.

---

### 3. Service layer for owner creation

There is **no dedicated `create` method**; owner persistence goes through `saveOwner`.

**Interface:** `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/service/ClinicService.java` (declares `saveOwner(Owner)`)

**Impl:** `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/service/ClinicServiceImpl.java` (lines 232-237)

```java
@Override
@Transactional
public void saveOwner(Owner owner) throws DataAccessException {
    ownerRepository.save(owner);
}
```

The service is a thin pass-through. **All owner-creation business logic lives in the REST controller** (`addOwner`).

**Controller file (the real "create"):** `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`, method `addOwner(OwnerFieldsDto)` (lines 113-157). It normalizes address/telephone, rolls the registration date to a business day, enforces daily-limit / telephone-in-use / household-in-use / city-capacity rules, then sets the derived fields and saves:

```java
if (sharesHousehold) {
    owner.setHouseholdId(householdId(owner.getLastName(), owner.getAddress()));
}
...
owner.setCustomerCode(nextCustomerCode(owner.getCity(), owner.getLastName()));
owner.setNamesakeCount(namesakeCount(owner.getFirstName(), owner.getLastName()));
owner.setBulkSignupWarning(isBulkSignup(owner.getRegistrationDate()));
this.clinicService.saveOwner(owner);
```

Key private helpers in the same controller:
- `householdId(lastName, address)` (lines 313-327): first 12 UPPER-case hex chars of SHA-256 of `normalizedLastName + "|" + normalizedAddress`.
- `namesakeCount(firstName, lastName)` (lines 228-235): count of existing owners with same normalized first+last name.
- `isHouseholdInUse(lastName, address)` (lines 287-293), `normalizeName(...)` (lines 299-304), `nextCustomerCode(...)` (165-172), `isDailyLimitReached` (180-185), `isBulkSignup` (194-199), `toBusinessDay` (205-210), `isCityAtCapacity` (216-221), `toE164` (246-265), `isTelephoneInUse` (272-279).

Note: nothing here computes household **size** or sets a tier — `membershipTier` is only ever derived later via the entity getter.
